newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank says too early to change money policy.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank says too early to change money policy.

text.p: A Slovak government decision to put funds from the import deposit plan into the central bank (NBS) does not mean a change in monetary policy will occur immediately, NBS Governor Vladimir Masar said on Tuesday.

Last month NBS Governor Vladimir Masar said the bank might ease its strict monetary policy if funds collected from the import deposits were held by the NBS and thus drain liquidity from the banking sector.
"Our further attitude towards the influence of these funds on monetary policy will depend on how they will be used," Masar said after the government session.
Masar said the NBS expected the overall amount of the deposits "not to exceed 10 billion crowns" in the first half of this year. He declined further comment on the issue.

As of May 5, importers in Slovakia have been forced to place 20 percent of the price of selected consumer goods imported to Slovakia on deposit at a Slovak bank on an interest-free account period for six months.
